standard_prerequisites.name: Characterisation of effective Cartier divisors locally as V(f) with f a nonzerodivisor
A nonzerodivisor is not contained in a minimal prime of a reduced ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring, used at proof lines 8561-8563

core_obligations: Reduce to the statement about an effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 8549-8552).
Pass to an affine cover and write the divisor as V(f) with f a nonzerodivisor (proof lines 8552-8557).
Rule out f lying in a minimal prime by the algebra lemma (proof lines 8557-8563).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a closed subscheme Z of a scheme X with blowing up b : X' -> X, the map b induces a bijection from the generic points of irreducible components of X' to the generic points of irreducible components of X that do not lie in Z (source lines 8540-8547). The proof reduces to the statement that for an effective Cartier divisor D in a scheme S no generic point of an irreducible component of S lies in D: it replaces S by an affine cover, writes D = V(f) with f a nonzerodivisor, and derives a contradiction from f lying in a minimal prime by the corresponding algebra lemma.
